correctness.rationale: The actual frozen six-blob Git tree reconstructed exactly to 120fe93f0b866193a1f20b763b71f89815d1f3cf and main returned identical six blob IDs. For the real norm N(x,y)=[|x|^3+((|x|+|y|)/2)^3]^(1/3), the analytic global quadratic comparison with H(x,y)^2=x^2+3^(-4/3)y^2 reduces, including both coordinate axes, to F(t)=[(8+(1+t)^3)/8]^(2/3)/(1+3^(-4/3)t^2) for t>=0. Its endpoint values both equal m=3^(4/3)/4; d(log F)/dt/2 has sign of R(t)-3^(-4/3) where R(t)=(1+t)^2/[t((1+t)^2+8)]. Symbolic differentiation independently confirms R'(t)=-(t+1)(t^3+3t^2-5t+9)/[t^2(t^2+2t+9)^2], and t^3+3t^2-5t+9=t(t-1)^2+5(t-3/5)^2+36/5>0. There is one positive critical point tau, a global maximum M; Hilbert Ptolemy and mH^2<=N^2<=MH^2 give C_Pt<=M/m. Take nonzero distinct x=(-1,0), y=(0,-tau), z=x+y=(-1,-tau): by absolute norm, N(x-y)=N(z)=N(1,tau), while denominator N(x)^2+N(y)^2=[3^(4/3)+tau^2]/4, giving the exact M/m lower bound. Independent 60-digit root/ratio calculation gives tau=2.7667398800787011390685370499587 and C_Pt=1.29958204360103898476109693949. Thus the exact claim and equality witness are correct, with no finite-sample-to-infinite inference.
